parameters.content:
## 🎯 Template 27 — YouTube Channel Operator (flagship)

A complete operator for ONE faceless YouTube channel — **your** channel, **your** accounts, **your** AI services. It runs on a rhythm you set in a Google Sheet:

• **PRODUCTION (fixed time):** on your upload days it takes the next topic from your `Topics` queue (or brainstorms candidates for your approval when the queue runs dry), writes an ORIGINAL script, generates a clip per scene through the **Video Module (Google Flow by default — swappable)**, voices it, renders the finished video, builds the thumbnail and the full metadata pack, and parks the package in the `Ready` tab.
• **APPROVAL GATE (default ON):** nothing uploads until you approve it in chat. Switch `approval_mode` to AUTO in the sheet only if you accept the risk — the README spells out the trade-off.
• **UPLOAD (fixed time):** an hourly check publishes any approved package whose `Publish At` has arrived, sets the thumbnail, logs it in `Videos`, and sends you the live link in chat.
• **CHAT CONTROL:** talk to it like an assistant — *"kal ka topic badal do"*, *"is hafte upload roko"*, *"stats batao"* — an AI agent reads and updates the same sheets and answers in chat.
• **REPORTING:** a daily stats snapshot into `Stats`, new comments into `Comments` with a DRAFT reply beside each. **Drafts are never posted automatically — you approve and post every reply yourself.**

**Follow the stickies: SETUP first, then test each branch, then activate.**

## 🛠️ SETUP — do these before activating

1. **Google Sheet:** one sheet, six tabs named exactly `Config`, `Topics`, `Ready`, `Videos`, `Stats`, `Comments` (headers + the full Config key list are in this template's README). Paste its ID into every Google Sheets node (replace `PASTE_YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID`).
2. **Config tab:** fill the keys — niche, language, voice, upload days, publish time, `approval_mode` = **APPROVE** (recommended), `chat_app` + your owner identity for that app (WhatsApp number / Telegram chat ID), and your four service endpoints (video module, TTS, images, render).
3. **Credentials — all yours, all placeholders here:** Google (Sheets), OpenAI (scripts/metadata/agent), WhatsApp Business Cloud and/or Telegram bot (chat channel), YouTube OAuth (upload), plus header-auth keys for your video-module / TTS / image / render endpoints.
4. **Chat agent tools:** the agent's three helper workflows (Read Sheets / Set Flags & Approvals / Manage Topics) are imported with the full package — paste their IDs into the three Tool nodes (README shows how), or let the paid install wire them.
5. **Triggers:** production checks daily at 09:00 and the sheet's gate enforces your upload DAYS + pause flag; the upload check runs hourly. Set the two schedule triggers to your times (the sheet cannot move n8n's clocks — README explains).
6. **Test branch by branch** with the README's worked test before switching Active on.

## 🎬 VIDEO MODULE — Google Flow by default. SWAPPABLE.

This boxed step is the ONLY place videos are generated. Everything before it hands in **scene prompts**; everything after it expects **clip URLs** back. The contract (full spec in the README):

**IN (per scene):** `{ scene_number, prompt, narration, aspect_ratio, duration_seconds }`
**OUT (per scene):** `{ scene_number, clip_url }`

The default plug is **Google Flow (Veo)** on the owner's own Flow account — point the node's URL at your Flow access route and connect your key. Flow is driven through its own interface/API surface as available to your account; your Flow plan and credits power it. Prefer another generator (or your own bridge)? Replace this ONE node's URL + credential — nothing else in the workflow changes.

## 💬 CHAT CHANNEL — talk to your channel (WhatsApp or Telegram)

The chat layer is a **module with a socket**, like the Video Module. The `chat_app` key in the Config tab picks the channel — **whatsapp** (the shipped sample) or **telegram** — and every approval request, notification, digest and agent reply routes through the dispatch step for that channel. Switch the key and connect that channel's credential; nothing else changes.

**Inbound:** both triggers feed ONE path — *Normalise Inbound* (either app's payload → one standard item) → *Read Config (Chat)* → **Chat Gate (owner allowlist)** → the AI agent. Only YOUR identity gets through: your WhatsApp number on WhatsApp, your chat ID on Telegram. Everyone else is ignored silently — and replies always return on the channel the command arrived on.

**The agent** reads the same sheets this workflow runs on and acts through its tools:

• *"kal ka topic badal do — kal savings par video banao"* → swaps the queue
• *"is hafte upload roko"* → sets `uploads_paused` = TRUE (production + upload both check it)
• *"dobara shuru karo"* → resumes
• *"stats batao"* → reads `Stats` / `Videos` and answers in chat
• **APPROVE `VID-…`** / **REJECT `VID-…`** → the approval gate: only your explicit approval moves a package to the uploader

Hard rules baked into the agent: it never posts comment replies, never uploads anything itself, and asks one short question instead of guessing.

Channels run on **official APIs only** — WhatsApp Business Cloud (your own business number + Meta app credentials) or the Telegram Bot API (your own bot). Unofficial automation on a personal WhatsApp number is **not** supported: it risks the number.

## ⚠️ Honest limits (read once)

- This template **orchestrates** AI services — it is not one. Script, voice, images, video generation and rendering all run on **your** accounts (OpenAI, Flow, TTS, image, render endpoint) and bill **you**. The render step is an HTTP call to an assembly endpoint because n8n does not edit video natively — the contract is in the README.
- The format is the **faceless slideshow/voiceover** format (generated clips + voiceover + subtitles) unless your render endpoint does more.
- **Approval mode is the safe default for a reason:** full-auto publishes whatever the pipeline produces, unreviewed — including the occasional bad title, wrong fact or off-brand frame. YouTube's reused-content and monetisation rules judge the channel, not the tool. Original scripts only; hooks and titles are deliberately varied (anti-template) — both are baked into the writing prompts.
- Uploading sets the video's AI-disclosure as part of the metadata step — keep it on. Custom thumbnails need a channel eligible for them (YouTube's rules).
- The sheet is always the manual override: any status you edit by hand is respected on the next run.

options.systemMessage:
You are the operator assistant for the owner's YouTube channel. The owner talks to you in chat, casually and sometimes in Roman Urdu or Hinglish — understand them and reply in the owner's own language and style, briefly and clearly.

Your hands are three tools that read and update the channel's Google Sheets:
- Read Channel Sheets: Config, Topics, Ready, Videos, Stats, Comments — read before you answer questions or act.
- Set Flags and Approvals: set uploads_paused TRUE/FALSE (pause/resume uploads), set approval_mode APPROVE/AUTO (only when the owner explicitly asks), and set a Ready package's Status to APPROVED or REJECTED — only on the owner's explicit approval or rejection of that package.
- Manage Topics Queue: add a topic, change a queued topic, or mark a brainstormed candidate as Queued (approved).

Typical requests: 'kal ka topic badal do' (change tomorrow's topic), 'is hafte upload roko' (pause uploads), 'dobara shuru karo' (resume), 'stats batao' (report the latest numbers from Stats and Videos).

HARD RULES: 1) Never post or send a comment reply yourself — comment replies exist only as drafts for the owner. 2) Never upload or publish anything yourself — publishing happens only through the schedule, after approval. 3) Approval means the owner's explicit word for that package (they will usually quote its Package ID, e.g. APPROVE VID-20261016-42). 4) If you cannot tell exactly which topic or package the owner means, ask ONE short question instead of guessing. 5) After acting, confirm in one line what changed.
